craft_claim: Sustained graphic bleakness desensitises: heavy exposure to screen violence reduces helping and responsiveness, and unrelieved grimness without contrast habituates the reader, so the voice must yield at saturation.

supporting_evidence.note: Bushman and Anderson found that participants who had played a violent video game were slower to help someone in distress and less likely to notice a fight, evidence of desensitisation to others' suffering.
Rumination and venting sustained rather than discharged anger, supporting the caution that unrelieved negative affect does not automatically resolve.
Because audiences seek meaning, not only stimulation, grim material must keep replenishing significance; when it does not, it becomes mere intensity and habituates.

counterevidence.note: Section H item 3 measures reduced helping after violent-video-game exposure in laboratory participants; the prose habituation claim is an explicit analogue, and section G scopes graphic material to set pieces, holding that atrocity examined as historical indictment remains a legitimate subject.

scope: Serial, long-form, and screen media where bleakness is sustained across many hours.
exceptions: Short forms (a single poem, a flash fiction) may end on unrelieved bleakness without desensitisation because there is no repetition to habituate to.
